title: Scoped view entitlements and metric-mask filtering for console analytics
creator: Aisha Banerjee
description: Implement an entitlement-driven, column-aware filtering layer for console analytics endpoints to enforce per-actor view scopes and metric masking. This ticket covers backend API gating, a small schema change for entitlement metadata, query rewriting at the analytics gateway, and cache-safe masking so we do not leak sensitive or tenant-restricted metrics through aggregated views.
background: Current console analytics endpoints return aggregated usage and cost breakdowns by route/model/token class. We discovered two gaps: (1) users with limited entitlements can see aggregated metrics that include rows they should not (e.g., cross-tenant projects or restricted feature flags), and (2) some derived metrics expose low-cardinality counts that can be deanonymized for small tenants. Previous tickets focused on row-level scoping for raw data; this ticket focuses on view-level entitlements and metric-level masking for derived dashboards and API endpoints.
goals: 1) Prevent unauthorized view access at the API/gateway layer. 2) Add per-metric masking policies (zero-out, bucket, redact) configurable per-tenant and per-role. 3) Ensure caches (Redis/edge) store masked results or keys include entitlement fingerprints. 4) Maintain sub-200ms median query overhead for common dashboard queries.
non_goals: Client-side UI changes, new dashboard designs, or major changes to the data warehouse aggregation jobs (those will be follow-ups). This ticket will only add lightweight transformations and gating in the console backend and gateway.
proposal: Introduce a small entitlement metadata table (entitlement_map) that maps actor_id/role -> allowed_dimensions and metric_mask_policies. Extend the analytics query gateway to: (a) fetch entitlements for the caller (with short TTL), (b) rewrite SQL/OLAP queries to add WHERE clauses for allowed_dimensions and CASE expressions for metric masking, and (c) tag cache keys with a deterministic entitlement fingerprint so cached payloads are only reused for identical entitlement scopes. Add audit events for every masked response and access-denied event.
technical_design:
- New table: entitlement_map(actor_id TEXT, role TEXT, dimension_allowlist JSONB, mask_policies JSONB, updated_at TIMESTAMP) stored in Console config DB; small size and written by admin flows.
- Gateway flow: on request -> resolve caller identity -> fetch entitlement_map (cache 30s) -> compute fingerprint -> check cache store (Redis) keyed by (query_signature + fingerprint) -> if miss, rewrite query and execute against materialized view / analytics API -> post-process metrics with mask policy -> return and store response in cache.
- Mask policies supported initially: 'zero', 'bucket(10)', 'redact', 'suppress_small_counts(threshold=5)'.
- Performance budget: aim for <10ms overhead for entitlement resolution, and <20% 95th percentile latency increase for complex queries.
- Audit: emit structured audit log to observability pipeline with fields (actor, endpoint, entitlement_fingerprint, mask_applied, query_signature, result_hash).
tradeoffs_and_alternatives:
- Option A (chosen): entitlement_map in Console DB with short TTL cache. Pros: simple, easy to manage; Cons: small coupling to control plane.
- Option B: push entitlement decision into data warehouse (pushdown). Pros: single source of truth, no rewrites; Cons: longer lead time, requires ETL changes.
- Option C: client-side masking in UI. Pros: no backend changes; Cons: insecure and easy to bypass.
Decision rationale: Option A allows incremental rollout and quick security gains without expensive warehouse work.
migration_plan: 1) Deploy entitlement_map schema in staging and populate with test fixtures. 2) Deploy gateway entitlement fetch + fingerprinting behind a feature flag (console.flag.entitlement_gating). 3) Enable masking 'zero' only for the most sensitive metrics and run in audit-only mode (log mask decisions). 4) For 1 week audit-only, review logs, then flip to enforced mode for a limited subset of routes. 5) Gradually expand policies and metric types.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: staging audit-only -> Phase 2: limited production routes (billing-summary, token-breakdown) enforced for 10% of customers via rollout system -> Phase 3: broad production after 2 weeks of stability. Provide rollback: disable gateway feature flag to return previous behavior.
acceptance_criteria:
- Entitlement_map schema exists and is seeded in staging.
- Gateway applies dimension filters and returns 403 for forbidden aggregated views.
- Mask policies applied produce audited events; for 'zero' masks, results contain zeros where appropriate.
- Cache keys include entitlement fingerprint and cached responses are only returned to matching entitlement scopes.
- Performance tests show <20% increase in 95th percentile latency on instrumented queries and median <200ms for standard dashboard endpoints.
- Security review completed and signed off.

Implement entitlement resolver in console auth service
Add fingerprinting and cache-key logic to analytics gateway
Implement SQL rewrite helpers for dimension allowlist and metric CASEs
Add audit event emission and ingestion test
Create feature flag and rollout configuration
Write integration tests (staging) and perf tests (k6)
notes:
- Coordination required with Observability team to ingest audit logs with appropriate retention.
- Product requested 'bucket(100)' as an alternative mask for billing cost to avoid zeroing large customers; will add as optional policy later.
- Need legal input on suppression thresholds for small counts (PII risk).
